items.title: Section: A Deficient Officiating Side Also Bars Ordination — And the Lighter Conditions for Lay and One-Day Precepts

items.zh: 由此六因，不應授彼苾芻律儀。又除闕減能作羯磨阿遮利耶、鄔波拕耶、住清淨戒圓滿僧眾。問：由幾因緣，不應授彼近事男律儀？答：略由二因。一、意樂損害故；二、男形損害故。若意樂損害者，當知一切不應為受。若男形損害者，或有為受，然不得說名近事男。不說因緣，前已具辯。若近住律儀，當知唯由意樂損害不應為受。何以故？或有隨他轉故，或有為得財利恭敬，詐稱欲受近住律儀，然彼實無求受意樂，當知是名意樂損害。
items.en:
Second, insufficiency on the officiating side. Ordination is further withheld if the assembly lacks a qualified officiant capable of conducting the ceremony, a qualified preceptor, or a sufficient assembly upholding pure precepts.
Second, lay restraint; first, the question. Question: for how many reasons should lay restraint not be given? Second, the answer; first, stating and listing. Answer: for two reasons, in brief: first, damaged motivation; second, damaged male form.
Third, one-day restraint; first, stating the reason. One-day restraint should be known as withheld only for damaged motivation. Second, explaining why. Why is this so? Because some merely go along with another's urging, or falsely claim to wish for the one-day precepts purely to gain material support and respect, while having no actual wish to receive them at all — this is called damaged motivation.

items.zh: 若無如所說不應受因緣，當知應受如前所說所有

items.title: Section: Five Ways Monastic Precepts Are Relinquished — From a Sincere Change of Heart to Death Itself

items.zh: 律儀。問：有幾因緣，苾芻律儀受已還捨？答：或由捨所學處故，或由犯根本罪故，或由形沒二形生故，或由善根斷故，或由棄捨眾同分故。苾芻律儀受已還捨。
items.en:
Second, clarifying relinquishment; first, monastic restraint; first, the question. Question: for how many reasons are monastic precepts, once received, subsequently relinquished?
Second, the answer; first, stating the kinds. Answer: through relinquishing the training itself, through committing a root transgression, through the loss of male form resulting in an ambiguous condition, through the severing of one's own wholesome roots, or through relinquishing one's class of sentient beings, that is, at death — monastic precepts, once received, are subsequently relinquished.

items.title: Section: An Age Too Degenerate Even to Ordain — Why Precepts Already Received Still Persist

items.zh: 若正法毀壞、正法隱沒，雖無新受苾芻律儀，先已受得，當知不捨。所以者何？由於爾時穢劫正起，無一有情不損意樂能受具戒，況當有證沙門果者。
items.en:
Second, a careful clarification; first, stating it. When the true dharma has collapsed or vanished, though no one may newly receive monastic restraint, one should know that precepts already received previously are not thereby relinquished.
Second, the question raised. Why is this so? Third, the explanation. Because, at such a time, when the degenerate age is in full force, there is not a single being whose motivation remains undamaged enough to receive full ordination, let alone attain the fruit of a renunciant.

items.title: Section: How Lay and One-Day Precepts Are Relinquished — And "Expressed and Unexpressed Karma" Reaches Its Close

items.zh: 若近事男律儀，當知由起不同分心故，善根斷故，棄捨眾同分故，受已還捨。若正法隱沒時，如苾芻律儀道理，當知近事男律儀亦爾。若近住律儀，當知由日出已後，或由發起不同分心，或於中間捨眾同分，雖已受得，必復還捨。
items.en:
Second, lay restraint; first, stating its kinds. Lay restraint, once received, is subsequently relinquished through the arising of a mind no longer aligned with the vow, through the severing of one's own wholesome roots, or through relinquishing one's class of sentient beings, that is, at death.
Second, extending the exception. When the true dharma has vanished, the same principle explained for monastic restraint should be known to apply equally to lay restraint.
Third, one-day restraint. One-day restraint, once received, is subsequently relinquished once the sun has risen, through the arising of a mind no longer aligned with the vow partway through, or through relinquishing one's class of sentient beings in the interval, that is, through death during the observance.

items.title: Section: The Attainment of No-Thought Begins — Stilling the Mind Itself as a Mistaken Path to Peace

items.zh: 復次，云何無想定？謂已離遍淨貪，未離上貪，由出離想作意為先故，諸心心所唯滅靜、唯不轉，是名無想定。此是假有，非實物有。
items.en:
Third, the two mindless attainments; first, distinguishing each individually; first, the attainment of no-thought; first, subsumed under concentration; first, the question posed. Furthermore, what is the attainment of no-thought?
Second, the explanation; first, clarifying its establishment. One who has become free of attachment to the third absorption, yet not free of attachment to the absorption above it, taking the aspiration to transcend perception as primary, causes mind and its mental factors to simply cease and no longer function — this is called the attainment of no-thought.
Second, distinguishing whether it is provisional or real. This is merely provisionally existent, not any substantially real entity.

items.zh: 當知差別略有三種。一、下品修，二、中品修，

items.title: Section: The Superior Grade Never Retrogresses — And the Heretic Who Slandered the Dharma at the Moment of Death

items.zh: 三、上品修。若下品修者，於現法退，不能速疾還引現前。若生無想有情天中，所得依身不甚清淨、威光赫奕、形色廣大如餘天眾。定當中夭。若中品修者，雖現法退，然能速疾還引現前。若生無想有情天中，所感依身雖甚清淨、光明赫奕、形色廣大，然不究竟最極清淨。雖有中夭，而不決定。若上品修者，必無有退。若生無想有情天中，所感依身甚為清淨、威光赫奕、形色廣大，又到究竟最極清淨。必無中夭，窮滿壽量後方殞沒。復次，若由此因此緣，所有生得心心所滅，是名無想。
items.en:
Third, the superior grade; first, never retrogressing. Whoever cultivates it to the superior grade never retrogresses at all. Second, an extremely pure body. Whoever is reborn in the heaven of no-thought through this grade receives an embodiment of the utmost purity, radiant and vast, reaching the very summit of purity. Third, never dying prematurely. Such a being never dies prematurely, only passing away once the full allotted lifespan is exhausted.
Second, subsumed under rebirth. Furthermore, through this cause and this condition, the resulting cessation of mind and its mental factors at birth is called no-thought.

items.title: Section: The Attainment of Cessation — A Noble One's Own Deeper Stillness, Reaching Even Into the Seventh Consciousness

items.zh: 復次，云何滅盡定？謂已離無所有處貪，未離上貪，或復已離。由止息想作意為先故。諸心心所唯滅靜、唯不轉，是名滅盡定。此定唯能滅靜轉識，不能滅靜阿賴耶識。
items.en:
Second, the attainment of cessation; first, the question posed. Furthermore, what is the attainment of cessation?
Second, the explanation; first, clarifying its establishment. One who has become free of attachment to the sphere of nothingness, yet not free of attachment to the sphere above it, or one who has become free of that attachment as well, taking the aspiration to bring mental activity to rest as primary, causes mind and its mental factors to simply cease and no longer function — this is called the attainment of cessation.
Second, distinguishing what actually ceases. This attainment can only still the active consciousnesses, not the store-consciousness.

items.title: Section: Three Grades of This Deeper Stillness — and Why Only Some Arhats Can Actually Enter It

items.zh: 當知此定亦是假有，非實物有。此定差別略有三種。下品修等，如前已說。若下品修者，於現法退，不能速疾還引現前。中品修者，雖現法退，然能速疾還引現前。上品修者，畢竟不退。有學聖者能入此定。謂不還身證。無學聖者亦復能入，謂俱分解脫。
items.en:
Third, distinguishing whether it is provisional or real. One should know that this attainment, too, is merely provisionally existent, not any substantially real entity.
Fourth, extensively distinguishing its kinds; first, referring back. This attainment's distinctions are, in brief, of three kinds — the lower grade and the rest, as already explained before.
Second, a comprehensive analysis; first, subsumed under the attainment of cessation. Among those still in training, the non-returner who has achieved direct bodily realisation can enter this attainment.
Among those beyond further training, this attainment can likewise be entered — namely, by the one liberated in both respects.

items.title: Section: Why No Noble One Ever Enters the Attainment of No-Thought — And Xuánzàng's Refusal to Abbreviate a Single Word

items.zh: 前無想定，非學所入，亦非無學。何以故？此中無有慧現行故。此上有勝寂靜住及生故。又復此定不能證得所未證得諸勝善法，由是稽留誑幻處故。
items.en:
Second, subsumed under the attainment of no-thought; first, stating it. The attainment of no-thought discussed earlier is entered by neither those in training nor those beyond training. Second, the question raised. Why is this so?
Third, the explanation; first, because it involves no wisdom. Because no wisdom manifests within this attainment.
Second, because something more excellent exists above it. Because more excellent tranquil abidings and rebirths exist above this attainment.
Third, because it is not the right place to rest. Because this attainment cannot bring about any excellent wholesome quality not yet attained, since it merely detains the practitioner in a deceptive, illusory state.

items.title: Section: Space Is Simply the Absence of Form — Neither Real Object Nor Real Function, Like Every Unconditioned Phenomenon

items.zh: 復次，虛空云何？謂唯諸色非有所顯，是名虛空。所以者何？若處所行都無所得，是處方有虛空想轉。是故當知此唯假有，非實物有。
items.en:
Fourth, the two unconditioned phenomena; first, space; first, the question posed. Furthermore, what is space?
Second, the explanation; first, clarifying its establishment; first, stating it. Space is simply what is revealed by the mere absence of form. Second, the question raised. Why is this so? Third, the explanation. Wherever no activity of form whatsoever is found, precisely there does the notion of space arise.
Second, distinguishing whether it is provisional or real. Therefore one should know that space is merely provisionally existent, not any substantially real entity.

blocks.text: How vows end, and two deep meditative states that look alike but are very different: the "attainment without perception" (無想定), a non-Buddhist dead end, and the noble "attainment of cessation" (滅盡定).
If none of the bars described apply, one may receive the precepts. (Untranslated, 0592b26.)

subs.head: Five ways to relinquish monastic vows

blocks.text: Giving up the training, a root transgression, change of sex with an ambiguous condition, severing wholesome roots, and death. Master Cháng Bǎi: in the first, the monk himself declares it.
No one can newly receive the monastic vow then, but what was received earlier is not lost.
The one-day vow ends when the sun rises, when a contrary mind arises, or at death. Master Cháng Bǎi: after twenty-four hours, at sunrise, it is relinquished.

The meditator, having left attachment to the third meditation, aims to leave perception; mind and mental factors simply stop. Master Cháng Bǎi: he thinks perception disturbs his stillness. It is provisional: only the first six consciousnesses temporarily stop. (Untranslated, 0592c16: it has three grades.)

The superior grade does not regress; rebirth there is radiant and long. Master Cháng Bǎi: but the seventh and eighth consciousnesses, with self-grasping, are still there. Thinking this is liberation is overweening pride.
A noble attainment. Master Cháng Bǎi: here even the seventh consciousness, with its view of self, ceases; but not the eighth, or this body would die.
Among learners, the non-returner with bodily realisation; among arhats, the one liberated both ways. Not every arhat qualifies.
No wisdom appears in it; better states exist above it; and it cannot bring any new good quality. Master Cháng Bǎi stresses the first: there is no wisdom there.
"Space is simply what is revealed by the mere absence of form." It is merely provisional.
Two silences: one is wisdom stopping, the other is wisdom completed. From outside they look the same.

quiz.q: By what five causes are monastic precepts, once received, relinquished?
options: relinquishing the training, a root transgression, loss of form with both forms arising, severed wholesome roots, abandoning the class of beings
relinquishing the training, breaking minor training rules, drinking intoxicants, leaving the community, and abandoning the class of beings
a root transgression, the vanishing of the true dharma, a teacher's death, a dissolved community, severed roots
faithlessness, laziness, forgetfulness, distraction, and corrupted wisdom
quiz.why: The treatise lists relinquishing the training, committing a root transgression, loss of male form with an ambiguous condition, severing of wholesome roots, and abandoning the class of beings. Master Cháng Bǎi on the first: the monk himself decides to give up the training received, that is, his original vow. The vanishing of the true dharma is expressly said not to cause relinquishment.

quiz.q: The English has "through death itself" for 棄捨眾同分. What are the gains and losses?
options: the sense is wrong: this class is the community, and the phrase means disrobing, not death
the sense is wrong: this class is the vow, and the phrase means breaking it, not death
nothing is lost: the literal words mean death, and no comment is needed
the sense is right, for the lecture says death; but the literal "abandoning the class of beings" and its link to the earlier term are lost
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: or through the end of life, for the monastic precepts last until death. So "through death itself" gives the right sense as a free rendering. What is lost is the term: 眾同分 was rendered "the class of sentient beings" in the previous fascicle, and a reader of the English cannot see that death is here conceived as leaving that class.

quiz.q: When the true dharma collapses or vanishes, what happens to monastic restraint, and why?
options: new reception is still possible, while what was received before is lost
new and old alike are lost, and all monks become lay people
neither is affected, and all continues as usual
no one newly receives it, but what was already received is kept, since in that age no being has undamaged motivation to receive it
quiz.why: The treatise says that though no one can newly receive monastic restraint, what was received earlier is not relinquished. The reason given for no new reception: in that degenerate age not one being has undamaged motivation for full ordination, let alone attains a renunciant's fruit. Master Cháng Bǎi: no being's motivation remains undamaged. The same is said for lay restraint.

quiz.q: Under what circumstances is one-day restraint relinquished once received?
options: after noon, after a meal, or on sleeping partway through
a root transgression, the loss of form, or severed roots
leaving the temple, returning home, or staying with family
after the sun has risen, on arising of a mind not aligned with the vow, or on death partway through
quiz.why: The treatise names three causes: the sun having risen, the arising of a mind not aligned with the vow, and abandoning the class of beings partway through. Master Cháng Bǎi: after twenty-four hours, once the sun has risen, the vow is relinquished; and if one suddenly dies during the observance, it is relinquished as well. Severed roots are listed for lay restraint, not here.

quiz.q: How does the treatise define the attainment of no-thought?
options: free of attachment to the sphere of nothingness but not above it, with the aim of resting first, mind and factors simply cease and do not function
with all afflictions severed, wisdom of selflessness removes perception forever
free of attachment to the third absorption but not above it, with the aim of leaving perception first, mind and factors simply cease and do not function
a beginner's mind free of idle thoughts for a while, awareness remaining
quiz.why: The treatise defines it by what has been left, namely attachment to the third absorption's level, and by the aim of leaving perception, with mind and mental factors simply ceasing and not functioning. Master Cháng Bǎi: the mind and factors of the first six consciousnesses temporarily do not manifest. The second option is the definition of the attainment of cessation.

quiz.q: The English has "the attainment of no-thought" while 想 in the same sentence is "perception." What effect does this have on the reader?
options: no effect: thought and perception are two different factors here and rightly differ
one term has two renderings, hiding that what is stopped is the perception of the aggregate; the lecture says he thinks perception disturbs the mind
the English is better: this stops discursive thought and has nothing to do with the aggregate
the English makes a state with perception into one without, reversing the sense
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: he thinks "perception" disturbs his mind and keeps him from abiding in clear stillness. This is the same 想 as the perception aggregate discussed later in the fascicle. Rendering the attainment "no-thought" while its aim is "to transcend perception" hides the link, so an English reader cannot see that the attainment stops exactly what the aggregate of perception names.

quiz.q: "This is merely provisionally existent." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain this of the attainment of no-thought?
options: because the eighth consciousness too stops, leaving no substance
because it is an outsiders' idea that the Dharma does not accept
because it is only a state in which the first six consciousnesses pause for a while
because the practitioner is only asleep, with body and mind stopped, and no real absorption exists
quiz.why: The treatise says this attainment is provisional, not a substantially real entity. Master Cháng Bǎi: that is because it is only a state in which the first six consciousnesses temporarily stop. It is thus designated on a phase of the mental stream, like the other mind-dissociated phenomena, and is not a further entity. The seventh and eighth consciousnesses have not stopped.

quiz.q: What results follow from cultivating no-thought at the superior grade?
options: it may regress; rebirth brings an inferior body; death may come at any time
it never regresses; no rebirth follows, and one enters final nirvāṇa at once
it never regresses; rebirth brings an utterly pure, vast body; there is no premature death, and one passes away only when life is exhausted
it never regresses; rebirth is in the formless realm, bodiless, for eighty thousand eons
quiz.why: The treatise says the superior grade never retrogresses; rebirth in the heaven of no-thought gives an embodiment of the utmost purity, radiant and vast; and there is no premature death, only passing away when the lifespan is exhausted. Master Cháng Bǎi: such a person's absorption is very stable, with mastery in entering and leaving it. Purity of body here is not liberation.

quiz.q: Why does Master Cháng Bǎi warn about the attainment of no-thought?
options: the seventh and eighth remain, with self-grasping; it is a stone on grass, and mistaking the state brings overweening pride
the eighth also ceases in it, so one may be unable to return
it brings powers, which leave one open to possession by spirits
it first requires severing all afflictions, which ordinary beings cannot do
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the mind and factors of the first six consciousnesses do not manifest, yet the seventh and eighth are still there, with self-grasping. Overweening pride means mistaking the state and claiming what is not realised. Thinking of nothing is only a stone pressing on grass, like cutting grass without removing the root, for it grows again with the spring wind.

quiz.q: The English has "the aspiration to bring mental activity to rest" for 止息想作意. According to the Sub-commentary, what is 止息想?
options: the thought of abiding for a while in liberation; the English "mental activity" differs and does not render 想
the thought of ending all consciousness forever; "to rest" understates it
turning away from all perception and seeking no-thought, which the English "mental activity" exactly fits
the thought of resting the body; the English turns body into mind
quiz.why: The Sub-commentary says that the thought of abiding for a while in liberation is called 止息想, and Master Cháng Bǎi adds that this is an attainment of noble ones only. The contrast with no-thought lies here: no-thought turns away from perception, while cessation aims at a temporary liberation. The English "bring mental activity to rest" loses that, and 想 is left unrendered.

quiz.q: How do the attainments of no-thought and cessation differ in what ceases, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: no-thought also stops the seventh; cessation stops only the first six
both stop only the first five, mental consciousness continuing
both stop all eight, so rebirth follows on leaving them
no-thought stops only the first six; cessation also stills what is joined with the seventh's view of a person-self
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the attainment of no-thought is only the ceasing of mind and factors of the first six consciousnesses, whereas in the attainment of cessation even the mind and factors of the seventh, joined with the view of a person-self, are stilled. The treatise's limit holds for both: only the active consciousnesses are stilled, never the store-consciousness.

quiz.q: Why can the attainment of cessation not still the store-consciousness?
options: the treatise says only active consciousnesses are stilled; were the eighth to cease, the ripened body would die
the store-consciousness is an undying self, so it never ceases
noble ones in compassion keep it in order to save beings
the store-consciousness appears only at buddhahood, so in absorption there is none of it to still
quiz.why: The treatise states that this attainment can only still the active consciousnesses. Master Cháng Bǎi supplies the reason: if the eighth consciousness were destroyed, this ripened body would die, so the eighth cannot be made to stop functioning. That is how one in this attainment differs from a corpse.

quiz.q: Which noble ones can enter the attainment of cessation?
options: all those in training and all those beyond training
among those in training, the non-returner with direct bodily realisation; beyond training, the one liberated in both respects
only buddhas; arhats and non-returners cannot
stream-enterers and once-returners can; non-returners and arhats need not
quiz.why: Among those in training the treatise names the non-returner with direct bodily realisation, and among those beyond training the one liberated in both respects. Not every arhat qualifies. Master Cháng Bǎi: one who has only severed afflictive obstruction without severing obstruction to absorption cannot enter it; one who has severed both is called liberated in both respects.

quiz.q: Why do neither those in training nor those beyond training enter no-thought? What does Master Cháng Bǎi stress among the three reasons?
options: it is harder than cessation, so noble ones cannot manage it
it has no wisdom of selflessness, only a stone on grass, and cannot realise the uncontaminated path
it belongs to the desire realm, which noble ones have left
the heaven of no-thought is too short-lived and lies too low for noble ones to wish to be reborn in it
quiz.why: The treatise gives three reasons: no wisdom manifests in it, more excellent abidings and rebirths exist above it, and it cannot bring about any excellent quality not yet attained. Master Cháng Bǎi stresses wisdom: the absorption has no wisdom of selflessness and is only a stone pressing on grass, so it cannot realise the uncontaminated path. Hence the treatise's phrase, a deceptive place of delay.

quiz.q: How does the treatise define space, and is it substantially real?
options: it is a real, all-pervading entity, a really existing unconditioned phenomenon independent of form
it is a fifth great element beyond the four, a real form
it is revealed by the mere absence of form; it is provisional, not substantially real
it is a colour seen by eye-consciousness, a real sense-base of form
quiz.why: The treatise says space is simply what is revealed by the mere absence of form: wherever no activity of form is found, the notion of space arises. Therefore it is merely provisional. Master Cháng Bǎi: space is established relative to the presence or absence of form, and so it is provisional and not substantially real, though it is counted among the unconditioned.
